mainTopic: Forbidden and permitted fuels for the שבת lamp (balsam sap, טבל טמא, נפט לבן, the תוספתא's debate on oils), ending with tree-based materials and linen for טומאה and סכך
overview: This amud continues the discussion of fuels that may not be used for the שבת lamp. First, the גמרא explains that balsam sap is forbidden for two reasons: it is dangerous because it flares up (עף), and there is also a גזירה that a person might take some for himself. A short story about a mother-in-law shows how dangerous balsam oil is, and a verse about the poor people left to gather balsam and trap the חלזון is explained. Next, a ברייתא forbids lighting with טבל טמא and נפט לבן even on a weekday. The danger of נפט לבן is clear, and a verse teaches that טבל טמא is forbidden because a כהן may use impure תרומה only after it has been separated. The גמרא then quotes the full תוספתא, where תנאים argue about which fuels are allowed, from רבי טרפון's 'olive oil only' to רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule that only fuels the חכמים named are forbidden. The amud ends with a ברייתא saying that tree-based materials, except linen, cannot become טמא as cloth and may be used as סכך. אביי begins to comment on this, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not give the simpler reason: it is dangerous?
steps.stepSummary: The questioner asks why the earlier ruling about balsam sap was not explained by the simple fact that it catches fire easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Master say instead: it is forbidden because it 'flies' (it is volatile and flares up).
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the reason that was just given for not lighting with balsam sap. He suggests a more obvious reason: the substance is volatile and dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation was a rabbinic decree that a person might take some of the fuel for himself. The questioner points out that a much plainer reason already exists, namely physical danger. Why reach for a גזירה when safety explains the rule by itself?

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Master say (a polite way of suggesting a different explanation)
Because it 'flies', meaning it is volatile and flares up or catches fire quickly

phrases.english: Let the Master say: because it is volatile (it 'flies').
phrases.notes: Addressed to the one who gave the decree-based reason on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given on the previous amud for not lighting with balsam sap.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decree-based reason (שמא יסתפק ממנו) for forbidding balsam sap
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler, physical reason (danger) is available, so why use a rabbinic decree?

steps.title: Two reasons were intended: danger and a decree
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that both reasons apply: the sap is dangerous, and there is also a decree against taking from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was saying one reason and then another. One: because it is volatile. And another: a decree, in case a person takes some of it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the speaker never rejected the danger reason. He meant two reasons together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The format 'חדא ועוד' means 'first this, and also that.' Danger is reason number one. The decree that a person might take from the expensive fuel is an extra, second reason. So the question falls away, since nothing was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: He said one reason and then another
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest he take some of it for his own use

steps.whatToRemember: Balsam sap is forbidden for two reasons: it is physically dangerous (עף), and there is a גזירה that one might take from it.

phrases.english: He was saying one reason and another:
One: because it is volatile.
And another: a decree, lest he take some of it for himself.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reasons are combined, not replaced
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree reason was given instead of the danger reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree reason was given in addition to the danger reason.

steps.title: Story: a mother-in-law and the balsam oil
steps.stepSummary: A story shows how dangerous balsam oil is. A woman who wore it went to light a lamp, caught fire, and was burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a mother-in-law who hated her daughter-in-law. She told her: 'Go adorn yourself with balsam oil.' She went and did so. When she came back, the mother-in-law told her: 'Go light the lamp.' She went and lit it. Fire blew onto her and consumed her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short, tragic story that shows how flammable balsam oil really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the first reason from step 2, that balsam is עף. The oil on her body caught the flame of the lamp, and the fire spread onto her. The danger is real, not theoretical.

phrases.aramaic: הַהִיא חֲמָתָא דַּהֲוָת סָנְיָא לַהּ לְכַלְּתַהּ,
phrases.english: There was a certain mother-in-law who hated her daughter-in-law;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לַהּ: זִיל אִיקַּשַּׁיט בְּמִשְׁחָא דַּאֲפַרְסְמָא.
phrases.english: she said to her: Go adorn yourself with balsam oil.
She went and adorned herself.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתַא[י] אֲמַרָה לַהּ: זִיל אִיתְלַי שְׁרָגָא.
phrases.english: When she came, she said to her: Go light the lamp.
She went and lit the lamp.
Fire blew onto her and consumed her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא חֲמָתָא דַּהֲוָת סָנְיָא לַהּ לְכַלְּתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the danger reason (עף) mentioned in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Balsam oil is highly flammable and truly dangerous near a flame.

steps.title: The poor who were left behind: balsam gatherers and snail trappers
steps.stepSummary: Because balsam came up, the גמרא quotes a verse from ירמיהו and explains it. The 'vinedressers' were balsam gatherers, and the 'husbandmen' were trappers of the חלזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And of the poorest of the land נבוזראדן the chief of the guard left some as vinedressers and husbandmen.' 'Vinedressers': רב יוסף taught that these are the balsam gatherers, from עין גדי to רמתא. 'Husbandmen': these are the trappers of the חלזון, from the cliffs of צור to חיפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side topic connected to balsam. It explains who the poor people left in the land after the Destruction actually were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses farming words, but רב יוסף explains them as two specific jobs. One is gathering balsam in the south, and the other is catching the חלזון (the source of תכלת dye) in the north. These were simple gathering jobs that the poorest people were left to do.

keyTerms.meaning: The poorest people of the land
The sea creature used to make תכלת dye

phrases.english: 'And of the poorest of the land Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard left'
'to be vinedressers and husbandmen' (Jeremiah 52:16).
'Vinedressers': Rav Yosef taught,
these are the gatherers of balsam,
from Ein Gedi to Ramata.
'Husbandmen': these are the trappers of the chilazon snail,
from the Promontory (Ladder) of Tyre to Haifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדַּלַּת הָאָרֶץ הִשְׁאִיר נְבוּזַרְאֲדָן רַב טַבָּחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion triggered by the mention of balsam in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the verse, 'כורמים' means balsam gatherers and 'יוגבים' means חלזון trappers.

steps.title: ברייתא: no lighting with impure טבל or white naphtha, even on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not light with טבל טמא or with נפט לבן even during the week, and certainly not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one may not light with impure untithed produce during the week, and needless to say not on שבת. Similarly, one may not light with white naphtha during the week, and needless to say not on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of forbidden fuels by quoting a ברייתא that lists two fuels forbidden every day of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both fuels are banned even on a weekday, so the problem is not specific to שבת. Saying 'needless to say on שבת' teaches that if the fuel is forbidden on a weekday, it is surely forbidden on שבת. This sets up the next question about the reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been taken
White naphtha, a highly flammable petroleum oil

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a שבת-only rule. Both fuels are forbidden even on a regular weekday, so the reason must be something that applies every day.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not light with impure tevel during the week,
and needless to say on Shabbat.
Similarly:
One may not light with white naphtha during the week,
and needless to say on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story and verse to the main topic of forbidden fuels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טבל טמא and נפט לבן may not be used for lighting, even on a weekday.

steps.title: White naphtha makes sense, but why impure טבל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that נפט לבן is forbidden because it is dangerous, but asks what the reason is for forbidding טבל טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for white naphtha, because it is volatile. But impure tevel, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first ruling in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer, which comes in the very next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נפט לבן is easy to explain, because like balsam it is עף and dangerous. טבל טמא is not dangerous at all, so a different reason is needed. Since it is impure and cannot be eaten anyway, why not burn it? The next step answers this question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable regarding... (sets up a contrast)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא נֵפְטְ לָבָן — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא עָף,
phrases.english: Granted, white naphtha: because it is volatile;
but impure tevel, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא נֵפְטְ לָבָן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא עָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why burning טבל טמא is forbidden, since it poses no danger.

steps.title: A verse shows that impure תרומה may only be used after it is separated
steps.stepSummary: The verse speaks of two kinds of תרומה. Just as pure תרומה belongs to the כהן only after it is separated, impure תרומה may also be used only after separation. So טבל טמא, which still holds unseparated תרומה, may not be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My תרומות." The verse is talking about two kinds of תרומה: pure תרומה and impure תרומה. Pure תרומה belongs to you only from the time it is separated and onward. In the same way, impure תרומה belongs to you only from the time it is separated and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6: why may one not light with טבל טמא? It brings a verse to show that the כהן's right to use impure תרומה begins only once it has been separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן may burn impure תרומה for light. But the plural word "תרומותי" teaches that impure תרומה follows the same rule as pure תרומה: it belongs to the כהן only after הרמה. טבל has not been separated yet, so nobody may burn it, not even a כהן, and not even during the week.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says (a source from the תורה is being brought)
The charge of My תרומות (plural, so two kinds)
Impure תרומה, which may not be eaten but may be burned by a כהן
From the moment of separation and onward

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think טבל טמא is forbidden because of שבת. It is forbidden even on a weekday, because the תרומה inside it has not been separated yet, so no one has the right to use it.

phrases.english: The verse said:
"And I, behold, I have given you
the charge of My terumot"
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:ח. The plural form is the key to the derivation.

phrases.english: The verse speaks of two terumot:
one is pure teruma
and one is impure teruma.
Just as with pure teruma
you have rights in it only
from the time of separation and onward,
so too with impure teruma
you have rights in it only
from the time of separation and onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 about why טבל טמא is forbidden.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כהן's right to benefit from impure תרומה begins only after הרמה. טבל has not been separated, so burning it is forbidden.

steps.title: Back to the תוספתא: no lighting with צרי, which is balsam sap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the original תוספתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids lighting with צרי, and he explains that צרי is simply the sap of the balsam tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the text itself. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: one may not light with צרי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also used to say: צרי is nothing more than sap from balsam trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The word "גופא" tells us the גמרא is returning to quote the full תוספתא it mentioned earlier. It begins with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling against lighting with צרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source behind the earlier discussion of balsam (Steps 2-4). רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds a side fact: צרי, one of the spices in the קטורת, is only sap that drips out of the tree. It is not part of the tree itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The text itself: the גמרא returns to quote a source in full
Balsam resin, one of the spices of the קטורת

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
One may not light with tzori,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would also say:
Tzori is nothing but
sap from balsam trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טבל טמא topic and returns to quote the full balsam תוספתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not light with צרי. צרי is merely balsam sap.

steps.title: Three תנאים narrow which fuels may be used
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל forbids anything that comes from a tree. רבי ישמעאל בן ברוקה allows only what comes from fruit. רבי טרפון allows only olive oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: one may not light with anything that comes out of a tree. רבי ישמעאל בן ברוקה says: one may light only with what comes out of fruit. רבי טרפון says: one may light only with olive oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The תוספתא lists three more opinions. Each one limits lighting more strictly than the last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל forbids all tree products, such as sap. רבי ישמעאל בן ברוקה goes further and allows only fruit oils, so non-fruit fuels are out. רבי טרפון is the strictest: only olive oil.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes out of the tree (e.g., sap)
What comes out of the fruit (fruit oils)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Anything that comes out of the tree,
one may not light with it.
Rabbi Yishmael ben Beroka says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹצֵא מִן הַפְּרִי.
phrases.english: One may light only with what comes out of the fruit.
Rabbi Tarfon says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: One may light only with olive oil alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the תוספתא with stricter opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three views, each stricter: no tree products; only fruit products; only olive oil.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי protests: what will people in other lands do?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי stands up and objects. Babylonia, Media, Alexandria, and Cappadocia each have only sesame oil, nut oil, radish oil, or naphtha. A rule that allows only olive oil would leave them with nothing to light with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי stood up and said: What will the people of Babylonia do? They have only sesame oil. What will the people of Media do? They have only nut oil. What will the people of Alexandria do? They have only radish oil. What will the people of Cappadocia do? They have neither of these, only naphtha.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי attacks the strict views, especially רבי טרפון's. He uses rhetorical questions to show that those views would leave whole communities unable to light. This sets up his own rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These questions are not asking for information. They are a challenge: a ruling that leaves most of the Jewish world with no legal fuel cannot be right. Standing up shows how strongly he objected.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood on his feet (a strong, public objection)

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri stood on his feet and said:
What shall the people of Babylonia do,
who have only sesame oil?
And what shall the people of Media do,
who have only nut oil?
And what shall the people of Alexandria do,
who have only radish oil?
And what shall the people of Cappadocia do,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם לֹא כָּךְ וְלֹא כָּךְ, אֶלָּא נֵפְטְ?
phrases.english: who have neither this nor that, but only naphtha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the restrictive opinions of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The restrictive views, especially רבי טרפון's olive-oil-only rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a rule would leave entire communities with no permitted fuel, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule: only what the חכמים listed is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי concludes that no oil is forbidden except the ones the חכמים specifically named.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the only forbidden fuels are the ones about which the חכמים said: one may not light with them.
steps.whatsHappening: After his protest, רבי יוחנן בן נורי gives his own lenient rule. Only the fuels listed as forbidden are forbidden, and everything else is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reverses the approach of Step 9. Instead of listing what is allowed, we start from "everything is allowed" and forbid only the specific items the חכמים named, such as those in the משנה of במה מדליקין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This lenient approach matches the practical הלכה that most oils may be used for the נר שבת, except those specifically excluded.

phrases.english: Rather, you have only
what the Sages said, "one may not light" with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the positive rule that follows from his protest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the fuels the חכמים explicitly forbade are forbidden. All others are permitted.

steps.title: More permitted fuels: fish oil, tar, gourd oil, and naphtha
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא permits fish oil and tar. רבי שמעון שזורי adds gourd oil and naphtha. סומכוס says that of animal products, only fish oil may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may light with fish oil and with tar. רבי שמעון שזורי says: one may light with gourd oil and with naphtha. סומכוס says: one may not light with anything that comes from flesh, except fish oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The תוספתא continues by listing more fuels that are allowed. This sets up the גמרא's question about סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first, unnamed opinion (the תנא קמא) permits fish oil. סומכוס seems to say the same thing, just in the form of a general rule about animal products. That apparent overlap is what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: And one may light with fish oil and with tar.
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
One may light with gourd oil and with naphtha.
Sumchos says:
Anything that comes from flesh,
one may not light with it,
except with fish oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the תוספתא with further permitted fuels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish oil and tar are permitted. רבי שמעון שזורי adds gourd oil and naphtha. סומכוס allows no animal product except fish oil.

steps.title: Isn't סומכוס saying the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what סומכוס adds, since the תנא קמא also permits fish oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't סומכוס's view the same as the first תנא's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two opinions in the תוספתא look identical, and it asks what the difference between them is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the תנא קמא and סומכוס allow fish oil. If they truly agree, there is no reason to record סומכוס separately. So there must be a practical difference.

phrases.english: Sumchos is the same as the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the apparent redundancy in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference exists between סומכוס and the תנא קמא?

steps.title: They argue about רב ברונא's ruling, but we don't know who holds which side
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is רב ברונא's ruling in the name of רב, about melted fat mixed with oil. But it is not clear which of them permits it and which forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: the ruling of רב ברונא in the name of רב. But it is not defined which one holds which view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions really do argue about something practical: רב ברונא's ruling. However, we cannot tell which side each one takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ברונא said in the name of רב that melted fat with oil added to it may be used for lighting. One of these תנאים agrees and the other disagrees. The tradition did not preserve which one is which. The words "ולא מסיימי" mean exactly that: their positions are not identified.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
And it is not defined which one holds which view

steps.whatToRemember: The תוספתא gives a wide range of views on שבת fuel, from olive oil only up to רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule that only the fuels the חכמים named are forbidden. סומכוס and the תנא קמא differ only about fat mixed with oil, and we do not know which side each one takes.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for which one permits and which one forbids. The גמרא itself says this is unknown.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
regarding what Rav Beruna said in the name of Rav,
phrases.notes: Melted fat with oil added to it may be used for lighting.

phrases.english: but it is not defined who holds which view.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about רב ברונא's ruling on melted fat mixed with oil, but which side each one takes is not known.

steps.title: Tree-based materials cannot become impure as cloth, except linen
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rules that anything that comes from a tree is not treated as a three-by-three piece of cloth for טומאה, so it may be used as סכך. פשתן is the exception. The amud then ends with 'אמר אביי', which introduces a statement that continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, anything that comes from a tree does not count as a three-by-three piece of cloth, and one may use it to roof a סוכה, except for linen. אביי said: (his words continue on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sorts tree-based materials by whether they can become טמא as cloth. The last words, 'אמר אביי', set up the next move: אביי is about to explain this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A piece of woven cloth normally becomes able to receive טומאה once it measures three fingers by three fingers. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says material that grows from a tree does not get this status, so it cannot become טמא. Since סכך must be made of something that cannot become טמא, this material is kosher for סכך. פשתן is the exception: it counts as real cloth, so it can become טמא and may not be used as סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever comes out of a tree (plant-based material)
Three by three fingerbreadths: the smallest size of cloth that can become טמא
One may use it as סכך (the roof of a סוכה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the oils discussion just before it. This ברייתא is about טומאה of cloth and about סכך, not about lighting. The two rules are connected because something that can become טמא is not valid as סכך.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that פשתן has a special status compared with other plant materials. אביי's statement on the next amud builds on this.
